newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: P.Telecom talks to other partners despite alliance.
newsitem.headline: P.Telecom talks to other partners despite alliance.

text.p: Portugal Telecom said that it was still talking to other international partners about the possibility of taking a stake in the company despite having opted for the Anglo-U.S. Concert as its global partner.
Chairman Murteira Nabo told a news conference that such talks were continuing.
"PT is still talking to other partners about taking a stake in the company at the third phase of its privatisation," the chairman said.
He was speaking at a news conference to announce Portugal Telecom's decision to join the Concert alliance led by British Telecom and MCI.
Portugal Telecom board member Miguel Horta & Costa told Reuters that an announcement could be made during this week on the additional partners.
Murteiro Nabo said that one potential partner was Brazil's Telebras. "We would like to have Telebras as a shareholder, as we are already partners in the Atlantic Alliance," he said.
The Atlantic Alliance is a joint venture between the Portuguese company and the Brazilian concern.
The next phase of the privatisation of Telecom, in which the state still holds 51 percent, is set for the autumn.
